description: Charge-conjugation orbit structure on H_n blocks, measuring how many independent values a C-invariant total-isospin label may take at the pair layer (n=2) versus the forced six-strand two-nucleon layer (n=6). Marks the limit of the n=2 impossibility proof. Audit-only; exact combinatorics; no fit.
tier: exploratory (scope boundary of a corpus proof)

preregistered_reading.orbits_eq_1: C-invariant T constant; C alone closes the layer
preregistered_reading.orbits_ge_2: C alone does not close the layer; the n=2 proof is special

result.verdict: The pair-layer impossibility does NOT extend. At n=2 there are 2 blocks in 1 C-orbit, so a C-invariant T is CONSTANT — which is exactly PairIsospinAssignment's result, and C alone closes that layer. At n=6 (the forced six-strand two-nucleon carrier) there are 11 blocks in 6 C-orbits (1 self-conjugate: (3, 2, 1)), so a C-invariant T has 6 independent values available and is NOT forced constant. CONSEQUENCE: the n=2 proof is special to the two-block case and must NOT be quoted as closing the six-strand channel layer. What binds at six strands is the separate crossing-budget bound (R <= s^2 = 9 vs nature's 33.7), not charge conjugation. Two layers, two different obstructions — neither subsumes the other.
